title: Sustaining Faith Through Repeated Business Setbacks
paragraphs: After his third business venture failed within five years despite careful planning and genuine effort each time, Bimo began questioning whether his repeated setbacks reflected some deeper flaw in his character or judgment that he had somehow failed to recognize.

A religious mentor gently challenged this interpretation, noting that repeated difficulty did not necessarily indicate personal deficiency, and that attributing every hardship to personal failing reflected a subtly distorted theological framework rather than sound understanding.

This reframing helped Bimo distinguish between reasonable self-reflection, examining what specific lessons each failure genuinely offered, and unproductive self-condemnation that falsely equated hardship with divine disapproval or fundamental personal unworthiness.

Approaching his fourth venture with this clearer distinction in mind, Bimo maintained both realistic self-assessment and genuine trust in Allah's wisdom simultaneously, recognizing that repeated difficulty and divine care were not mutually exclusive possibilities.
